approach: Integrate the time-varying acceleration to get the velocity as a function of time and check whether it stays along the original direction of v.

steps.text: Integrate each component of a with respect to time, using the given velocity v = 2î at t = 0 as the starting values.
At t = 0 the velocity is (2, 0), matching the given v, but for any t greater than 0 the velocity has picked up a nonzero y component.
steps.equation: v(t) = (2 + 2t²) î + (t³/3) ĵ, nonzero ĵ component for t > 0

steps.text: Since the particle starts moving purely along x but develops motion along y as time passes, it is no longer confined to a straight line.
steps.equation: path curves away from the x-axis for t > 0
steps.why_this_step: A particle whose velocity direction changes over time (other than reversing along the same line) traces a curved path.

final_answer.value: Curvilinear (two-dimensional) motion, since the particle develops a velocity component along ĵ while it started moving purely along î.

common_mistakes.text: Noting that v is given only along î at t = 0 and concluding the motion stays one-dimensional, without checking that the acceleration has a persistent ĵ component that builds up a y-velocity over time.
